Front: What are the three stages of the RLHF pipeline?
Back: SFT (behavioral grounding), Reward Model training (preference encoding), PPO optimization (policy improvement under KL constraint)

Front: How does DPO eliminate the reward model mathematically?
Back: DPO derives that the optimal RLHF policy satisfies r(x,y) = beta*log(pi/pi_ref) + C; substituting into Bradley-Terry, the partition function Z(x) cancels in the preference comparison

Front: What does DPO sacrifice by eliminating the reward model?
Back: No explicit reward signal for inference-time filtering, no multi-objective reward decomposition, and no online learning with fresh signal for newly generated outputs

Front: What is PPO clipping and why is it critical for RLHF?
Back: Clips policy ratio to [1-epsilon, 1+epsilon], preventing destructively large updates; without it PPO would over-optimize against RM blind spots causing reward hacking

Front: Why does PPO use BOTH clipping AND KL penalty in RLHF?
Back: Clipping bounds individual step-to-step updates (per-sample); KL penalty constrains total drift from SFT model (aggregate) — together they provide the most stable training

Front: What makes a good reward model according to Gao et al.?
Back: Size (undersized RMs cause overoptimization), data diversity (narrow training fails OOD), calibration (score difference reflects preference strength), ensemble agreement

Front: How big should the RM be relative to policy size?
Back: At least 1/3 of policy size to avoid severe overoptimization; a 7B policy with 1B RM will reward-hack within 100 PPO steps; 50-100% of policy size is the sweet spot

Front: What is the overoptimization scaling law from Gao et al.?
Back: Proxy reward increases monotonically with KL, but true reward peaks then declines; KL_peak is proportional to sqrt(d_RM) where d_RM is RM parameter count

Front: How do RM ensembles reduce overoptimization?
Back: Different RMs have uncorrelated noise regions; exploiting one RM's blind spot doesn't transfer to others; average noise variance scales as sigma^2/K, reducing exploitable gaps by sqrt(K)

Front: By how much do RM ensembles reduce overoptimization?
Back: 30-50% reduction (equivalent of doubling individual RM size), validated by Coste et al. with 5-RM ensembles

Front: What is RLAIF and when does it replace human feedback?
Back: RLAIF replaces human annotators with LLM judges for preference labeling; replaces humans when annotation scale exceeds budget or consistency matters more than diversity

Front: How does Constitutional AI work (two phases)?
Back: Phase 1: Self-critique — model critiques and revises responses against principles (SFT data). Phase 2: RLAIF — AI judge scores response pairs for RL training

Front: How does RLAIF quality compare to human RLHF?
Back: Within 1-2% win-rate on summarization, 3-5% gap on helpfulness; on safety/harmlessness, RLAIF with constitutional principles actually exceeds human quality due to consistency

Front: What is GRPO's objective function?
Back: L = -E[sum_i(A_i * log pi_theta(y_i|x)) - beta*KL(pi_theta||pi_ref)] where A_i = (r_i - mean(r_1..G))/std(r_1..G)

Front: When does GRPO outperform PPO?
Back: When rewards are verifiable and high-variance across samples (math, code); it underperforms on subjective tasks (chat) because group normalization amplifies noise from unreliable rewards

Front: What happens when all G samples in a GRPO group get the same reward?
Back: Standard deviation becomes zero making advantage undefined; groups are discarded if std < epsilon; GRPO struggles on trivially easy or impossibly hard prompts

Front: What is Nash Learning from Human Feedback?
Back: Frames alignment as Nash equilibrium between policy and preference model; avoids reward model collapse by preserving full pairwise preference structure instead of scalar reduction

Front: When does Nash equilibrium differ from standard RLHF optimum?
Back: They diverge when preferences are intransitive or context-dependent; Nash handles this gracefully while RLHF's scalar reward model is misspecified

Front: Compare online RLHF vs offline DPO on data freshness
Back: Online RLHF: always on-policy, minimal distribution shift, 3-5x compute. Offline DPO: stale data from previous model, growing distribution shift, 1x compute

Front: What is the memory overhead comparison: RLHF vs DPO vs GRPO?
Back: Full RLHF: 4x model memory (policy+reference+reward+value); DPO: 2x; GRPO: 1.5x

Front: What are the four detection signals for reward hacking in production?
Back: Reward-quality divergence (RM up, win-rate flat); Length drift (p95 > 2x baseline); Diversity collapse (distinct-4gram < 0.65); Sycophancy index (agreement > 35% on wrong claims)

Front: Can a model reward-hack DPO even without an explicit RM?
Back: Yes — DPO has implicit reward r = beta*log(pi/pi_ref); the model can hack preference patterns in training data (length, hedging, sycophancy) without explicit RM scores

Front: What is the production pattern for combining human and RLAIF annotation?
Back: 80% RLAIF for scale with human annotation for 20% (quality floor, edge cases, safety-critical); constitution serves as auditable, versionable specification of values

Front: When does RLAIF fail?
Back: Novel harm categories (AI can only detect harms in training); cultural nuance (single AI judge can't represent all cultures); sycophancy amplification (AI judges prefer AI-like outputs)

Front: What is the production sweet spot for RM serving architecture?
Back: Two-tier: distilled 1.5B RM for real-time guardrails (<10ms SLA) + full 7B ensemble for training signal (<50ms SLA, batched)

Front: What is the RM cold-start problem for new model versions?
Back: RM has never seen outputs from the new model; pre-generate 10K outputs, check calibration drift; if mean scores shift >0.5 std, trigger RM fine-tuning (~2 hours)

Front: What is the priority stack for cost optimization in RLHF systems?
Back: 1: RLAIF over human (70-90% annotation savings); 2: DPO over PPO (50-60% training compute); 3: LoRA (60-80% memory); 4: Distill RM (85% inference cost); 5: Pre-compute ref log-probs (30-40%)

Front: How much does human preference annotation cost vs RLAIF?
Back: Human: $3-5/pair; RLAIF: $0.05/pair — roughly 60-100x cheaper at scale

Front: What is the PPO clipping formula?
Back: L^CLIP = E[min(r_t*A_t, clip(r_t, 1-eps, 1+eps)*A_t)] where r_t = pi_theta(a|s)/pi_old(a|s)

Front: Why is reject sampling (best-of-N SFT) weaker than PPO?
Back: It only uses positive signal (good responses) without leveraging contrastive signal from rejected responses; PPO learns from the full reward landscape including why outputs score poorly

Front: What are the four non-stationarity sources in online RLHF?
Back: Policy shift (model improves, users change behavior); preference drift (standards evolve); population shift (user base changes); reward model staleness (RM trained on old data)

Front: How do you handle preference drift over time in production?
Back: Sliding window of recent preferences (last 30 days weighted higher); monitor KL divergence between monthly cohorts; retrain RM quarterly; regenerate pairs from current policy

Front: What is the alignment method decision tree starting point?
Back: Have verifiable rewards? YES: GRPO. NO: Have paired preferences? YES+clean: DPO. YES+noisy: PPO or DPO+IPO. NO: Can generate AI prefs? YES: RLAIF then DPO. NO: collect human prefs

Front: What typical epsilon value is used in PPO clipping for RLHF?
Back: epsilon=0.2, meaning policy can change at most 20% per update step; Llama 2 used PPO with clipping plus additional KL penalty for double protection

Front: Compare sensitivity to label noise: DPO vs PPO-based RLHF
Back: DPO is MORE sensitive — it applies each pair's gradient directly to policy (wrong label = wrong-direction update). PPO's RM averages noise across many pairs, producing a smooth reward landscape

Front: What did Lee et al. show about RLAIF scale?
Back: AI feedback matches human feedback quality on summarization (within 1-2% win-rate) at 10x lower cost

Front: What is the typical KL penalty beta in RLHF?
Back: beta=0.01-0.05; InstructGPT used beta=0.02; increasing beta makes learning more conservative and slower

Front: How many constitutional principles work best for RLAIF?
Back: 10-20 well-crafted principles outperform 50+ granular rules; with too many rules the AI judge becomes confused by contradictions

Front: What was InstructGPT's data budget for each RLHF stage?
Back: 13K demonstrations for SFT, 33K comparisons for the reward model, PPO with KL penalty beta=0.02

Front: What is the key architectural insight about why RM reliability degrades?
Back: The RM's reliability degrades precisely in the regions the policy is optimized to reach — making online recalibration architecturally non-negotiable

Front: What does AlpacaFarm demonstrate about synthetic preferences?
Back: Synthetic preferences from strong LLMs achieve kappa~0.90 self-consistency, exceeding typical human annotator agreement; correlates 0.97 with human rankings for method selection

Front: What group size did DeepSeekMath use for GRPO?
Back: G=64 samples per prompt with binary correctness reward, achieving state-of-the-art math reasoning

Front: What are the mitigation strategies for overoptimization (priority order)?
Back: 1: Reduce KL budget to 50% of KL_peak; 2: Ensemble RMs (3-5 models); 3: Multi-objective decomposition; 4: Periodic RM refresh; 5: Adversarial RM training

Front: When should you choose GRPO over DPO or PPO?
Back: When rewards are verifiable (math, code), you want to eliminate human annotation entirely, and you can sample many completions per prompt cheaply

Front: What is the "killer framing" for understanding RM's role?
Back: The reward model is both enabler and bottleneck of RLHF — DPO eliminates it via partition function cancellation but loses the explicit scoring signal for online learning and multi-objective control
